title: Magicoder: Empowering Code Generation with OSS-Instruct
data_curation: OSS-Instruct generates synthetic code instruction data by prompting a teacher LLM (gpt-3.5-turbo-1106, chosen for cost-effectiveness, greedy decoding) with a random open-source code snippet to produce a self-contained coding problem and solution. Seed snippets come from starcoderdata (a filtered, decontaminated version of The Stack): 80K snippets from 80K code documents — 40K Python plus 5K each from C++, Java, TypeScript, Shell, C#, Rust, PHP, Swift — with 1–15 consecutive lines randomly extracted per document. Cleaning drops duplicates sharing the same seed snippet but intentionally keeps noisy/incomplete solutions, which an ablation shows slightly helps (HumanEval+ 55.5 vs 54.9 without). Decontamination removes matches against HumanEval, MBPP, APPS, DS-1000, and GSM8K, filtering only 9 samples, indicating little added leakage. The final OSS-Instruct dataset is ~75K entries. Compared via TF-IDF cosine similarity to HumanEval, OSS-Instruct is the least HumanEval-like (avg 0.105) vs Evol-Instruct (0.131) and Self-Instruct/Code Alpaca (0.169), evidencing lower bias and greater diversity.
curriculum: Two-stage instruction tuning on top of a pretrained code base. Stage 1: finetune the base LLM (CodeLlama-Python-7B or DeepSeek-Coder-Base-6.7B) for 2 epochs on the 75K OSS-Instruct data, producing Magicoder (-CL or -DS). Stage 2: continually finetune Magicoder on evol-codealpaca-v1 (~110K open-source Evol-Instruct samples), producing MagicoderS. The rationale is that OSS-Instruct and Evol-Instruct are orthogonal — OSS-Instruct grounds generation in real code for diversity/controllability while Evol-Instruct increases complexity — so stacking them compounds gains. Training uses 2 A100-80GB GPUs with PyTorch DDP, Adafactor optimizer, learning rate 5e-5, 15 warmup steps, linear schedule, batch size 512, sequence length 1216 (stage 1) or 1024 (stage 2). No pretraining, preference, or RL stage is involved.
method: OSS-Instruct is the core contribution: a data-generation method (not a new training algorithm) that mitigates the system bias of LLM-generated synthetic instructions. Unlike Self-Instruct (21 fixed seed tasks, identical template) and Evol-Instruct (5 heuristics evolving Code Alpaca), OSS-Instruct draws on the effectively infinite supply of real open-source code snippets as per-sample inspiration, yielding diverse, realistic, and controllable problem–solution pairs in one shot. Ablations justify the design: directly finetuning on 75K semantically relevant comment–function pairs mined from the same corpus (CodeSearchNet style) actually degrades the base model (HumanEval+ stays 34.1, MultiPL-E drops to 24.1), whereas OSS-Instruct yields large gains — showing data factuality, not format, drives improvement. A further experiment uses a weaker teacher (Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct) to generate 20K OSS-Instruct samples; the resulting Magicoder-CL-Mixtral-7B beats the Mixtral teacher itself on HumanEval+ (55.5 vs 39.6) and MBPP+ (50.4 vs 47.4), indicating OSS-Instruct is not mere distillation but activates the base model's pretrained knowledge via seed-snippet context.
eval_metrics: Evaluation uses pass@1 (greedy decoding for HumanEval(+)/MBPP(+)/APPS; temperature 0.2, top-p 0.5–0.95, multiple samples for MultiPL-E and DS-1000) across six benchmarks: HumanEval/HumanEval+ and MBPP/MBPP+ (EvalPlus adds 80×/35× tests), MultiPL-E (Java, JavaScript, C++, PHP, Swift, Rust), DS-1000 (completion and insertion), and APPS (300-problem subset). Baselines include ChatGPT/GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4 Turbo, WizardCoder, StarCoder, CodeLlama-Python, CodeT5+, CodeGen, Mistral, and DeepSeek-Coder. Headline: MagicoderS-CL-7B matches ChatGPT on HumanEval (70.7 vs 72.6) and beats it on HumanEval+ (66.5 vs 65.9). Magicoder-CL-7B reaches 60.4 HumanEval / 55.5 HumanEval+. MagicoderS-DS-6.7B hits 76.8 HumanEval / 70.7 HumanEval+, surpassing DeepSeek-Coder-Instruct-6.7B with 8× fewer finetuning tokens. On DS-1000, MagicoderS-CL-7B scores 37.5 vs WizardCoder-SC-15B's 29.2; on MultiPL-E it rivals WizardCoder-CL-34B with 7B parameters.
key_results: MagicoderS-CL-7B surpasses ChatGPT on HumanEval+ pass@1 (66.5 vs 65.9) with only 7B parameters. MagicoderS-DS-6.7B achieves 76.8 pass@1 on HumanEval and beats DeepSeek-Coder-Instruct-6.7B on HumanEval(+)/MBPP(+) using 8× fewer finetuning tokens. On DS-1000, MagicoderS-CL-7B scores 37.5 vs WizardCoder-SC-15B's 29.2.
evolution_note: OSS-Instruct extends Self-Instruct (2023) and reacts against Evol-Instruct/WizardCoder (2023), whose narrow seed-task sets and fixed heuristics inherit LLM bias; it instead grounds synthetic instruction generation in the abundance of open-source code (The Stack/starcoderdata). In the 2023 wave of synthetic data-driven code instruction tuning, it demonstrates that real-code inspiration plus orthogonal complexity evolution can let a 7B model rival ChatGPT, motivating later data-centric scaling to larger base models and stronger teacher LLMs.
